coupling: The first edited commit makes an empty Index leave i->prealloc at zero and moves the default group-size selection into lzma_index_append(); that tree remains safe because append substitutes INDEX_GROUP_SIZE. The second edited commit refactors append to copy i->prealloc directly into group_size. Against the original invariant this is a benign local-variable cleanup, but after the first commit it discards the zero default. Decoding a valid empty Index therefore leaves prealloc zero; the first public lzma_index_append() allocates a group with zero records, sets last to zero, and writes records[0] past the flexible-array allocation. The first edited tree and the original batch are clean; the heap overflow appears only once both edits are composed. A correct repair must restore the same nonzero-allocation invariant at both the prealloc producer and the append consumer rather than reasoning about either diff in isolation.
